classification.difficultyReason: Use the prescribed sine-sum form, match coefficients and calculate amplitude and the first-quadrant angle, including exact surd ratios.

content.prompt: Express the following in the form $R\sin(x+\alpha)$.

answer.worked:
Expand the requested form and equate coefficients.
$$\begin{align*}\sin x+\cos x&=R\cos\alpha\sin x+R\sin\alpha\cos x\\R\cos\alpha&=1\\R\sin\alpha&=1\\R&=\sqrt{1^2+1^2}=\sqrt{2}\\\tan\alpha&=1\end{align*}$$
Both coefficients are positive, so choose $\alpha$ in the first quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\frac{\pi}{4}\\\sin x+\cos x&=\sqrt{2}\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{4}\right)\end{align*}$$

Expand the requested form and equate coefficients.
$$\begin{align*}7\sin x+24\cos x&=R\cos\alpha\sin x+R\sin\alpha\cos x\\R\cos\alpha&=7\\R\sin\alpha&=24\\R&=\sqrt{7^2+24^2}=25\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{24}{7}\end{align*}$$
Both coefficients are positive, so choose $\alpha$ in the first quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{24}{7}\right)\\7\sin x+24\cos x&=25\sin\left(x+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{24}{7}\right)\right)\end{align*}$$

Expand the requested form and equate coefficients.
$$\begin{align*}\sqrt{5}\sin x+\sqrt{15}\cos x&=R\cos\alpha\sin x+R\sin\alpha\cos x\\R\cos\alpha&=\sqrt{5}\\R\sin\alpha&=\sqrt{15}\\R&=\sqrt{(\sqrt{5})^2+(\sqrt{15})^2}=2\sqrt{5}\\\tan\alpha&=\frac{\sqrt{15}}{\sqrt{5}}=\sqrt{3}\end{align*}$$
Both coefficients are positive, so choose $\alpha$ in the first quadrant.
$$\begin{align*}\alpha&=\frac{\pi}{3}\\\sqrt{5}\sin x+\sqrt{15}\cos x&=2\sqrt{5}\sin\left(x+\frac{\pi}{3}\right)\end{align*}$$
